findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:55 — TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })` uses a translation key that was never added to apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json (verified via grep: zero matches), so AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43's `t(err.message)` will render the raw untranslated key to the end user instead of a message

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:173 — Success response `{ message: "Guests added" }` is a hardcoded, non-localized, untyped free-text string (unlike the keyed/translated error messages) and is not even consumed by the only current caller (AddGuestsDialog.tsx onSuccess shows its own toast and ignores the response body), making the return contract an unused, unstable ad hoc shape with no dedicated fields (e.g. success flag, updated booking) for future callers to rely on

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.min(1)`, so a caller invoking the endpoint directly (bypassing the web dialog's own client-side guard) with `guests: []` is accepted by validation and only fails downstream with the misleading BAD_REQUEST message "emails_must_be_unique_valid", which describes a different condition (duplicate/invalid emails) than "no guests supplied"
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max-length bound, so a single request can enqueue an arbitrarily large guest list.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — NOT_FOUND path when bookingId does not match any booking is untested.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:55 — TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })` uses a translation key that was never added to apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json (verified via grep: zero matches), so AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43's `t(err.message)` will render the raw untranslated key to the end user instead of a message

adjudication.rationale: The handler does throw `new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })` and the client does call `t(err.message)`, but the claim that `you_do_not_have_permission` is “never added to .../common.json” cannot be verified from this diff: the locale file is only shown as a partial snippet around unrelated keys, so the key may already exist elsewhere in that same file (or another loaded namespace). The finding relies on an external grep result not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:173 — Success response `{ message: "Guests added" }` is a hardcoded, non-localized, untyped free-text string (unlike the keyed/translated error messages) and is not even consumed by the only current caller (AddGuestsDialog.tsx onSuccess shows its own toast and ignores the response body), making the return contract an unused, unstable ad hoc shape with no dedicated fields (e.g. success flag, updated booking) for future callers to rely on

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the mutation ends with `return { message: "Guests added" };`, which is a hardcoded free-text string (not i18n-keyed like TRPCError messages) and an ad hoc response shape. In the only diff-shown caller (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`), `onSuccess` does not read the mutation result at all (it just toasts `t("guests_added")`, closes, resets, and invalidates), so this return contract is currently unused and provides no stable/typed fields for future callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.min(1)`, so a caller invoking the endpoint directly (bypassing the web dialog's own client-side guard) with `guests: []` is accepted by validation and only fails downstream with the misleading BAD_REQUEST message "emails_must_be_unique_valid", which describes a different condition (duplicate/invalid emails) than "no guests supplied"

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` without `.min(1)`, so `guests: []` passes input validation. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, an empty `guests` array yields `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is misleading for the "no guests provided" case. This is a verifiable behavior path introduced by the diff and results in incorrect error semantics for direct API callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max-length bound, so a single request can enqueue an arbitrarily large guest list.

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` bound. The handler then uses this array to `createMany` attendees and triggers calendar updates and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)` over `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`, so an unbounded array can cause excessive DB writes and email sends (DoS/resource exhaustion) from a single request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — NOT_FOUND path when bookingId does not match any booking is untested.

adjudication.rationale: This diff introduces a new mutation handler `addGuestsHandler` with an explicit NOT_FOUND branch (`if (!booking) throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "booking_not_found" });` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`). The PR diff shows no accompanying test additions/updates covering this new endpoint or its error paths, so the claim that the NOT_FOUND path is untested is a concrete, diff-grounded gap rather than a functional defect.
